deferred_findings.subject: Resolve Manila Line Philippine land endpoint
deferred_findings.current: No production convoy layer; observed label and cap in audit register
deferred_findings.notes: Entire sea path is traced, including P45 and the P51→P50 Philippine bend. The white-anchor-on-blue terminal is a major port, not a dockyard. It is drawn on the western Visayas island cluster; assignment to Luzon and the Visayas versus Mindanao is unresolved in the source interpretation. Do not infer the endpoint from the Manila label or proximity to the Mindanao label. Do not import as a complete usable route until the endpoint is resolved.

deferred_findings.subject: Baffin source conflict: blank glossary row versus earlier tundra assignment
deferred_findings.proposed: Reconcile blank intrinsic glossary row with current tundra and board ice artwork; see AM-232.
deferred_findings.notes: This is an actual source disagreement after visual glossary check, not an uninspected approach. It duplicates the more explicit AM-232 issue.

deferred_findings.subject: Impassable Amazon needs explicit non-normal adjacency treatment
deferred_findings.proposed: Trace Colombia/Ecuador/Venezuela approaches against the hatched border; do not add ordinary passable neighbors through the impassable artwork. Keep air, supply, and river legality distinct.
deferred_findings.notes: Entire western Amazonas boundary and both impassable-region tips were inspected. Venezuela and Bolivia have finite unhatched geographic contacts (current edge / AM-051 respectively); Colombia/Ecuador contacts and movement across the hatched tip remain source/model questions. Peru approach remains explicitly blocked by AM-072.

deferred_findings.subject: US–Canada map-seam contacts
deferred_findings.proposed: Alberta–Pacific Northwest and Alberta–Upper Midwest finite same-image borders are resolved by AM-241. Manitoba–Upper Midwest across opposite map cuts remains an uncertain candidate because the cut fragments do not align. Retain user-approved Alberta–Manitoba and Mackenzie–Keewatin.
deferred_findings.notes: Both seam fragments inspected; source-registration ambiguity is explicit. This no longer withholds the Alberta borders that can be seen on the same source fragment.

deferred_findings.subject: Mississippi river-route and directional crossing audit
deferred_findings.proposed: Printed Mississippi network is present through Midwest, Chicago, Heartlands, Appalachia, New Orleans and Texas; explicit combat directions have now been compared against glossary pp5–6. A rules-backed river-transport layer must represent channel continuity separately from river_crossing; see root mechanisms proposal.
deferred_findings.notes: River artwork and all explicit glossary directions were inspected. Residual uncertainty is the legal/channel encoding into has_river, not an unperformed visual search for blue lines. Canal/seaway routes and navigability are separate from merely sharing a river border.

deferred_findings.subject: Remaining US opposite-map-edge land borders

proposed.railway: trace each track across matched seam rows, do not infer from adjacent rails

deferred_findings.notes: Composite places opposite image edges side by side at unchanged vertical coordinate. User-approved Canadian seam decisions are not superseded. Finite row overlap suggests missing US edges, but unequal map art and gutter must be reconciled before creating links.

deferred_findings.subject: Clarify shore railway fields against whole-zone rail coverage
deferred_findings.current: Mostly false on existing legacy coast entries; several ports are attached to wrong seas
deferred_findings.proposed: Retain observed track/access artwork as evidence, but derive legal zone railway coverage using rulebook §13.2.8: a land zone with a border-crossing railway is covered by rail. Decide whether land-sea railway_connection stores artwork, legal access, or should be retired.
deferred_findings.notes: Corrected after rules QA: a dedicated spur to each naval facility must not be invented as an extra prerequisite. Visible tracks may document geography, but the game rule covers the entire zone.

deferred_findings.subject: Baffin Island glossary blank row versus ice artwork

proposed.board_artwork: white ice/glacier-looking interior; no printed tundra tree field

deferred_findings.notes: The earlier Canadian audit assigns tundra. Glossary p5 has no X for Baffin whereas Keewatin explicitly has tundra. Resolve source mismatch before changing a previously authored territory.

deferred_findings.subject: Interpret the Amazonas all-adjacent-territories river requirement
deferred_findings.proposed: Apply to every legal incoming approach after determining whether the source wording includes sea landings and whether a proposed land edge is actually passable.
deferred_findings.notes: Literal glossary p6 quantifier is preserved in the directional table. Hatched Amazon impassable artwork takes precedence over any assumption that a listed river penalty creates legal movement.

deferred_findings.subject: Remaining field-specific interpretation limits
deferred_findings.proposed: Every stored physical pair touching the reviewed regional land nodes was examined (three Iranian external borders are covered by AP), and the additional 19 regional sea pairs were examined. See the explicit pair ledger. Remaining unresolved fields are listed per pair; river-route and facility/gauge scope is not implied by physical-adjacency confirmation.
deferred_findings.notes: Second source pass replaced the first-pass blanket topology deferral. This is a proposal audit with field-scoped coverage, not full-field certification.

deferred_findings.subject: Impassable Sahara and Pripet boundary routing
deferred_findings.proposed: Author map-relative passability per crossing, preserving the distinction between physical adjacency and legal ground traversal. Do not delete all touching territories or set entire mixed zones impassable.
deferred_findings.notes: Shaded Sahara/Pripet areas cover parts of multiple named territories. Shortest within-two-zones route must be checked for each candidate border; rail lines across Pripet require explicit source/rules reconciliation, not automatic assumption.

deferred_findings.subject: Spain original nationality versus civil-war setup
deferred_findings.proposed: Use a consistent static Spanish identity and dated Nationalist/Republican setup allocation; verify setup sheet before changing faction ownership.
deferred_findings.notes: Current mix of Spain, Nationalist Spain and Republican Spain is inconsistent. Printed flags and the 1936 civil-war setup are not interchangeable with national identity.

deferred_findings.subject: Karelia river-table wording
deferred_findings.notes: Glossary says River Border with, whereas most rows say from. Trace both sides of each river; do not mechanically set both directions.

deferred_findings.subject: Southern Iran–Punjab printed rail gap
deferred_findings.proposed: Likely false; verify high-resolution endpoints and whether special rule joins them.
deferred_findings.notes: Iranian line stops west of frontier and Punjab line begins inland east of it. No continuous crossing is visible.

deferred_findings.subject: South China/India/Himalayan impassable boundary treatment
deferred_findings.current: Existing true defaults or incomplete endpoint edges

proposed.uncertainty: Whether to encode physical contacts hidden inside the broad impassable mountain band as geography-only edges or use a barrier-area layer. Kashmir/Sinkiang and Afghanistan/Sinkiang contact interpretation should not create passable moves.

deferred_findings.notes: The native second pass checks every stored Himalayan pair. Confirmed passable:false borders remain geographically present. The residual uncertainty is representation of the broad black barrier area and its hidden political contact lines, not an uninspected stored edge.

deferred_findings.subject: Kobdo–Novosibirsk tiny border and Tannu Tuva state identity
deferred_findings.current: Kobdo–Novosibirsk present; Tannu Tuva owned by Mongolia
deferred_findings.proposed: Confirm the narrow boundary junction and distinguish printed Tannu Tuva roundel from Mongolia setup affiliation.
deferred_findings.notes: Fresh native crop still leaves Kobdo–Novosibirsk tiny city-arc contact visually ambiguous. Tannu Tuva has a distinct red outer/blue inner emblem roundel, unlike Mongolia's white circle with upright emblem; original political identity versus player/home-country affiliation needs source reconciliation.

deferred_findings.subject: Glossary/map ambiguity: Vyatka self-reference and omitted Yugria
deferred_findings.current: Missing nodes; glossary says Vyatka river border from Vyatka
deferred_findings.proposed: Preserve raw citation; resolve which neighboring approach was intended by map trace or official errata.
deferred_findings.notes: Do not turn the apparent glossary typo into a self-loop or silently substitute Yugria.

deferred_findings.subject: Represent river transport separately from combat river crossings
deferred_findings.current: Many defaults; many uniform rail=true flags
deferred_findings.proposed: Use the complete physical, railway/gauge and directional glossary ledgers. Model named river transport as a continuous network with banks and route permissions; a combat river-crossing requirement is not sufficient to infer that network.
deferred_findings.notes: All 310 stored physical pairs and 64 proposed land/narrow pairs touching 36 new land tiles have now been source-checked for the relevant physical and railway/gauge questions. The remaining river transport item is a schema/representation decision, not a deferred physical-neighbor or railway review. Under §13.2.8 p98, any printed border-crossing railway gives whole-zone rail coverage; individual port spurs are not prerequisites.

deferred_findings.subject: Unlabeled USA roundel inside P27 has no identified land outline
deferred_findings.proposed: Retain the crop/provenance and resolve the symbol; do not invent a named island or ownership of the sea zone.
deferred_findings.notes: The USA roundel is clear, but no island outline, name, IPP or facility accompanies it. The terrain glossary does not supply a matching named tile. This is a real source ambiguity, distinct from an edge we have not yet traced.

deferred_findings.subject: Manchurian printed original identity is different from Japan control
deferred_findings.proposed: Preserve the Manchukuo printed roundel as original national identity; represent Japanese control separately according to rules/setup rather than silently replacing one field.
evidence: docs/map_audits/full_world/evidence/ap_east_asia.png; Rulebook §0.2 Home Country table includes Manchukuo roundels separately.
deferred_findings.notes: Roundels are legible. Remaining question is the intended schema meaning of original_owner and scenario controller, not uncertainty about which symbol is printed. Coordinate with global identity/setup proposal.

deferred_findings.subject: Remote British Pacific ownership allocation requires explicit reconciliation
deferred_findings.current: Existing Fiji/New Hebrides United Kingdom; added remote islands proposed FEC from terrain-table grouping
deferred_findings.proposed: Retain printed roundel and resolve Great Britain versus FEC player allocation using national setup; do not treat a terrain-table section heading as sufficient political state.
deferred_findings.notes: This is an allocation/model decision needing source reconciliation. Zero-IPP islands still matter to control, basing, home country and capture rules.

deferred_findings.notes: Fresh 2026-10-06 review confirms major_port type and P50 access but retains island-group ownership uncertainty. The naval ledger records one unassigned physical facility with two candidate land nodes, never one duplicate in each territory. No dockyard symbol is present.

deferred_findings.subject: P42–P50 open-water contact at the Philippine island-group divide
deferred_findings.notes: Native inspection resolves the neighboring P41, P42, P50 and P51 polygons but does not expose a finite P42/P50 open-water segment distinct from island outlines and the implicit Luzon/Visayas–Mindanao grouping. This is one of two unresolved stored physical pairs, with Kobdo–Novosibirsk.

deferred_findings.subject: Direct Saratov–Ural railway connection at the dense Volga junction
deferred_findings.current: Ural node absent; the newly proposed physical land border is real
deferred_findings.notes: The original artwork superimposes the Saratov/Gorky/Ural/Orenburg political boundaries, Volga tributaries and railway junction. Saratov-to-Ural direct passage versus an intervening short Gorky or Orenburg segment cannot be assigned confidently at native resolution. Nearby tracks have yellow broad-gauge checkers, but the direct edge remains unresolved. This is one source ambiguity among 64 reviewed new-node border rail cases, not uninspected work. Ural whole-zone railway coverage is independently established by its other confirmed rail borders.

uncertainties.details: The printed board clearly shows a white circled-anchor minor-dockyard symbol, while the supply-path example calls Cape Town a Minor Port. Expected facilities here transcribe the board symbol; reconcile edition/source precedence before applying a different type.

gauge_change.rule: Compare verified source_rail_gauge and target_rail_gauge on a confirmed railway; false if no railway, otherwise null.

printed_rail_coverage.rule: A land-border railway establishes whole-zone coverage; absence of such a record does not prove no internal railway.
